- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., 79.16 → 80.66 in Example 3), then undercorrects.
- Underestimates in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days), suggesting lag or delayed response to recent trends.
- Mean reversion bias: model fails to adjust downward after prolonged high prices, overestimating continuation.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually converge toward true values — suggesting a “warm-up” or “initial overconfidence” bias.
- High variance in forecast error near the end of the 30-day window, indicating model struggles with short-term volatility or horizon decay.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of the distribution — underestimates extreme high prices (e.g., 82.31) and overestimates low prices (e.g., 75.72 → 76.33).
